title: Model CD pipeline: signed artifact build + perf profile publishing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: Build a repeatable, auditable CI/CD pipeline that automates model onboarding artifacts (model binaries, manifest, provenance), produces signed artifacts, runs gated performance regression tests, and publishes verified performance profiles to the model catalog. Background: onboarding is currently manual: engineers push artifacts, run ad-hoc perf jobs, and request ops to promote. This causes delays, inconsistent metadata, and occasional regressions in production. Scope: 1) CI job(s) to build reproducible model artifacts from model repo tags and containerize runtime packaging. 2) Artifact signing integration with KMS/HSM and storage in the signed-artifacts bucket. 3) Automated perf regression suite (unit throughput/latency, KV-cache warmup tests, end-to-end latency p95 under representative load) run against a staging serving fleet. 4) Verification step that creates a performance profile object (quantization settings, kernel hints, sequence-length SLOs, cost estimate) and publishes to the model catalog with version pinning metadata. 5) Promotion workflow to move artifacts and profiles from staging -> canary -> prod with approval gates and automated rollback on regressions. Acceptance criteria: - A pushed model tag triggers pipeline and creates a signed artifact with provenance metadata (git sha, model hash, builder id). - Perf suite runs automatically; regressions fail the pipeline. - Successful pipeline run produces a profile entry visible in console/catalog and an immutable version pin that routing policies can reference. - Promotion requires at most 1 manual approval for production rollouts; rollback can be automated if production metrics deviate beyond threshold. - Audit logs are written for every promotion/sign operation and accessible to compliance. Implementation notes & trade-offs: - Use Buildkite for heavy GPU-enabled stages (existing runners) and GitHub Actions for fast orchestration steps to reduce maintenance surface. - Store artifacts in GCS signed bucket and replicate to S3 for multi-cloud retrieval; signatures use KMS HSM-backed keys per team. - To keep build times predictable, use incremental cache layers and deterministic builder images pinned by digest. - Perf tests use a mix of synthetic and replay trace inputs; prioritize quick smoke + full nightly runs to balance latency vs confidence. Rollout plan: 1) MVP pipeline for internal models (alpha testers) -> 2) extend to external model catalog entries -> 3) enable auto-promotion with canary traffic split. Monitoring and observability: pipeline metrics (build time, sign time, perf pass rate), model serving metrics during canary, and a perf-regression dashboard link in pipeline SMS. Rollback plan: pipeline captures artifact/manifest and automatically reverts routing pins on regression or manual rollback. Security/compliance: signing operations recorded; KMS key rotation policy enforced; secrets in CI via vault and ephemeral tokens. Dependencies: ENG-4729 for baseline build/sign promotion primitives; infra changes to add staging serving fleet for perf runs. Risks: flaky perf tests causing false failures; mitigations include deterministic inputs, synthetic replay, and test stability thresholds.
